title: Foundations: Creation
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: Introduction to the Foundations Series
subpoints: Overview of the 12-week series on essential doctrines
Emphasis on the practical application of theology to everyday life

outline.title: Historical and Confessional Basis for Creation
subpoints: The Apostles' Creed affirms God as the maker of heaven and earth
Westminster Larger Catechism Q14: God executes decrees in creation and providence
Westminster Confession 4.1: Creation ex nihilo for the manifestation of God's glory
Westminster Larger Catechism Q16: The creation of angels

outline.title: Biblical Testimony to Creation
subpoints: Genesis 1:1-3: The miraculous and sudden nature of creation by God's word
Exodus 20:11: The six days of creation as the basis for the Sabbath
Psalm 104:24: Creation displays the wisdom and goodness of God
Jeremiah 10:11-12: God's power and wisdom in establishing the world

outline.title: The Trinitarian Nature of Creation
subpoints: Ephesians 1:11: All things done according to the counsel of God's will
John 1:2-3: All things made through the Son
1 Corinthians 8:6: Father as source, Son as agent of creation
Hebrews 1:2-3: The Son sustains the universe by his powerful word

outline.title: Faith and the Reality of Creation
subpoints: Creation as a matter of faith rather than purely empirical proof
The necessity of divine revelation for acknowledging God as Creator

summary:
This sermon marks the beginning of the 'Foundations' series, a twelve-week study on essential Christian doctrines. The first lesson focuses on the doctrine of creation, establishing that God is the sole creator of all things, visible and invisible. The teaching emphasizes that this belief is not new but is rooted in the earliest Christian creeds and the Westminster Standards, which affirm that God created the world ex nihilo (out of nothing) for the manifestation of His glory, power, and wisdom.

The biblical basis for creation is explored through key passages such as Genesis 1, which depicts creation as a miraculous, sudden act of God's word, and Exodus 20, which links the six days of creation to the Sabbath commandment. The sermon highlights that creation displays God's wisdom and goodness, countering historical and modern views that devalue the material world. Furthermore, the text underscores the Trinitarian nature of creation, with the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit all involved in the act of making and sustaining the universe.

Finally, the sermon addresses the role of faith in understanding creation. While logical arguments can be presented, the ultimate acceptance of God as Creator is a matter of faith, as stated in Hebrews 11:3. The lesson concludes by affirming that the church has consistently held to the belief in a personal, sovereign God who created the world, distinguishing this view from ancient Greek philosophies that viewed the material world as eternal or evil.
